A few bits of code I've written over the years for fairly standard tasks that were annoying and time-consuming. I am confident in the accuracy of the code for my specific purposes, but **no warranty whatsoever** is offered for use elsewhere.

# Data cleaning

#### [Cleaning the Consumer Expenditure Survey](https://example.com)

<!-- placeholder description -->
Stata code that cleans the CEX following Aguiar and Bils (2015). Handles top-coding, multi-quarter aggregation across the interview and diary surveys, and the 2013 redesign. Outputs a household-quarter panel with consistent expenditure categories from 1996 onward.

#### [Cleaning the PSID](https://example.com)

<!-- placeholder description -->
R code that cleans the PSID following Guvenen and Smith (2014). Constructs annual measures of earnings, wealth, and consumption with consistent definitions across the biennial waves post-1997.

# Geography

#### [Linking historical UK geographies](https://example.com)

<!-- placeholder description -->
A Bash + Python pipeline that uses the ONS Geography Portal to crosswalk administrative geographies across boundary changes — parishes, wards, and LSOAs — with population-weighted apportionment for variables that don't aggregate cleanly.
